scope_basis: Additional financing for the West Africa regional digital integration programme: broadband infrastructure, online services and e-payments.
title: World Bank — WARDIP SOP1 additional financing, Mauritania, 2026
description: "Projet de loi autorisant la ratification de l'accord de financement, signée le 16 septembre 2026, entre la République Islamique de Mauritanie et l'Association Internationale de Développement (IDA), destiné au financement additionnel aux transformations numériques pour l'Afrique/ Programme Régional d'Intégration Numérique de l'Afrique de l'Ouest-SOP1(WARDIP). Le présent financement additionnel contribuera fortement à la réalisation de l'Agenda National de Transformation Numérique, notamment par la généralisation de l'infrastructure numérique haut débit accessible et de qualité et le développement de services en ligne et des paiements électroniques. Le présent prêt porte sur un montant de vingt-cinq millions huit cent mille (25 800 000) Euros, soit l'équivalent d'un milliard cent trente-six millions (1 136 000 000) MRU, remboursable sur une période de vingt (20) ans après un différé de cinq (5) ans, avec un taux d'intérêt de 1,5% par an, et une commission d'engagement de (0,5%) l'an sur le solde de financement non décaissé."

scope_basis: Surveillance system and command centre, but the grant also builds regional security service buildings and police observation posts.
title: Chinese Government provides MRU 629.4 million grant — via ETCA — for Urban Security and Monitoring System Project
description: In 2021, the Chinese Government and the Government of Mauritania signed a grant agreement worth 629,400,000 new ouguiyas (6.294 billion old ouguiyas) for the Urban Security and Monitoring System Project. The grant proceeds were drawn from an Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement (ETCA), which was previously signed by the parties. The purpose of this project is to construct a new video surveillance system and a Unified Command Center for the General Directorate of National Security in the capital city of Nouakchott. The video surveillance system consists of 316 surveillance cameras that can extend to as many as 1,000 observation points. The command center consists of a two-storey building built on an area of ​​500 square meters, three buildings for three regional security services (in each of the wilayas of Nouakchott), and 34 police station observation posts (including 30 posts in Nouakchott and 4 posts at the entrances to Nouakchott). Zhejiang Post & Telecommunication Construction Co., Ltd. (浙江省邮电工程建设有限公司) is the contractor responsible for implementation. A formal groundbreaking ceremony took place on May 4, 2021. The project was originally scheduled to begin implementation in April 2021 and reach completion in the second half of 2022.
